description: PIXEL DIFFS SAY «23 417 PIXELS DIFFER» AND LEAVE YOU TO FIND OUT WHY. This one says «the Submit button moved 8px down, its padding went 8 → 12, and it went disabled» — a sentence with a cause in it. op:"before" takes the state of the page as it is now; do the thing (a fix, a deploy, a click, a different branch); op:"after" compares. Reported: what appeared, what disappeared, and what moved, resized, changed state or changed a style that people argue about. Text content is deliberately NOT compared — a name, a total or a timestamp differs between two healthy runs, and reporting those is exactly the noise that gets visual diffing switched off everywhere else. Movements under 2px are the browser rounding a layout. When the two states cannot be matched at all — a virtualised list, a re-keyed render — it SAYS so instead of reporting three hundred false appearances.

draw.description: For "after": write a PNG here with every changed control outlined and labelled with what changed

omit.description: Drop these field paths and keep the rest — the cheap way to lose one huge field (["html"], ["steps"]) without listing everything you want.

op.description: "before" remembers this page; "after" compares against it; "drop" forgets it

select.description: Keep only these field paths, e.g. ["ok","fields[].name"]. Dots walk into objects, and a path through a list applies to every entry, keeping it a list. A path that matches nothing is reported back with the field names that ARE there.

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab

name: qa_diff
title: What changed on this page — by control, not by pixel
